Figure30.45A transmissionhologram is one that produces real and virtual images when a laser ofthe same type as that whichexposed the hologram is passed through it. Diffraction from various parts ofthefilm produces the same interference pattern as theobject that was used to expose it.

Since lasers produce coherent single-wavelength light, their interference patterns are more pronounced. The precision is so great that it is even possible to record numeroushologramson a single pieceoffilm by justchanging the angleof the film for each successive image. This is howthe holograms that move as you walk by them are produced—a kindof lensless movie.
